start: ^It was Friday afternoon, after school. Chris had just finished the homework he hadn’t completed the day before with his teacher and was about to head home.

^As he passed the art classroom, he spotted a girl sitting alone, staring intently at a sheet of paper. She was moving her pen across it, as though she were writing something. Curious, Chris stepped inside.
^Hey, what are you doing here all by yourself after school? Aren’t you going home?
^Startled by someone suddenly entering the room, the girl hurriedly began packing up her things, as though she were trying to hide something.
^Just as she was about to put away the sheet of paper, a sudden gust of wind blew it right in front of Chris. He picked it up.

^Chris took a closer look at the paper. It seemed to be a drawing of a riverside landscape, complete with a pond, mountains, grass, and lotus flowers. In the pond was a strange, polygon-shaped creature.
^If it isn’t yours, why did you have it?
^Then who drew it? It looks really nice.
^I never said you drew it. So what were you doing just now?
^Hahaha, relax. No need to be nervous.
cp01_o1: ^Really? But I just watched you working on that drawing for ages.
cp01_o2: ^B-because the person who drew it forgot to take it when they left. I was just going to write their name on it so nobody would mistake it for rubbish and throw it away.
^Is that so? But you’re the only person I’ve seen in here this whole time.
cp01_o3: ^M-my friend drew it. Pretty good, right? She just forgot to take it with her.
^It does look good. But why do you look so pleased about it?.
cp01_o4: ^B-because I wasn’t sure if this pen worked, I was testing it on a piece of paper.
^Oh, I see. I thought maybe you were jealous of someone else’s drawing and were about to ruin their work.
cp01_o5: ^I-I’m not nervous! You just startled me by barging in like that.
cp01_after: ^How long were you watching from outside?
^I saw you take that paper out of your bag. You drew it yourself, didn’t you?
^So you saw everything! Fine, I admit it. I drew it.
^So it really was yours! Actually, I didn’t see where you got the paper from at all. Hahaha!
^Hahaha, sorry, sorry! So why didn’t you want to admit that you drew it?
^Because I was afraid it didn’t look good. You saw it yourself, right? All the lines are crooked, and there are marks I can’t erase because I pressed too hard with the pencil.
^And it doesn’t really look like what it’s supposed to be.
^I actually think it looks really good.
^I’m sure you’ll get better if you keep practising.
^Only a few parts look a little odd. The rest is pretty good.
^As long as you enjoy drawing, that’s what matters.
^Then forget drawing and go play some sport! All your worries disappear when you exercise!
cp02_o2: ^If only I had that much time to practise.
cp02_o3: ^See! Even you think there’s something wrong with it!
^But that doesn’t stop the drawing from looking good overall?
cp02_o4: ^But I can never get my drawings right! How am I supposed to enjoy that?
^Then why not do something else that makes you happy?
^Out of all the things I want to do, drawing feels like the only one I can start and finish whenever I want.
^Wow, you really are short on time.
cp02_o5: ^My stamina is terrible. I’d be exhausted after just a few minutes. Besides, the worries would only go away temporarily.
^If you’re exhausted, that’s the perfect excuse to rest! And even if your worries only disappear for a little while, that’s better than worrying all the time.
cp02_after: ^Sigh... The truth is, my family doesn’t support me studying art seriously. They think it won’t help me get a job in the future.
^Huh? How can they be so sure what kind of job you’ll have?
^I guess they just want me to become a doctor or a lawyer.
^Could you give me my paper back? I’d like to draw a little more.
^Chris sat down beside Tracy, and they continued drawing and chatting.
^So, to make sure I can get into one of those careers they keep talking about, I have a private tutor come to my house every day after school.
^By the time I finish tutoring and all my school homework, it’s pretty much bedtime.
^My tutor couldn’t come today because something else came up, so the session was cancelled. They still left me homework, though.
^Classes finished early today too, so I finally got a chance to draw a little longer. To be honest, I almost don’t want to go home.
^You really love drawing, huh? If I had to study that hard, I’d probably go straight out with my friends instead, especially if school finished early. Speaking of which, where are your friends?
^They’re probably browsing around the supermarket on their way home. Or maybe they went to karaoke.
^Why didn’t they invite you? Doesn’t sound like a very close friendship.
^It must feel great not having tutoring today.
^Why not go join them? Spending time with your friends is important too.
^You and your friends have such different interests. Don’t people usually get influenced by those around them?
^So how long are you planning to stay here and draw?
cp03_o1: ^They did invite me, but I don’t really like group activities, so I turned them down.
cp03_o2: ^Yeah. Maybe if I had more days like this, I’d be better at drawing by now.
^You’re so keen to draw. I’m sure you’ll improve with time.
cp03_o3: ^We’re really just classmates who happen to be in the same classroom every day. Outside class, we all do our own thing. So we’re not actually that close. Haha.
^Well, if you can get closer to them, you should try. That way, if you ever need their help, it’ll be easier to ask.
^That makes a lot of sense. I’ll try!
cp03_o4: ^Maybe I’m one of the rare people who don’t get influenced that easily.
cp03_o5: ^Until a teacher comes to lock the classroom.
^Careful you don’t get locked in here by yourself.
cp03_after: ^Actually, there’s something I’ve been meaning to ask. What’s that polygon-shaped thing in the middle of your pond?
^Huh? I thought it was a rock.
^Nope. If you want to draw something accurately, you have to start with its outline and then gradually add the details inside it.'
^I see. Then how did you draw that mountain in the background?
^The mountain? That’s easy. The process is pretty similar to drawing the duck. The important thing is to make sure the peaks and dips in its outline don’t look too repetitive.
^For example, if one peak is 3 cm high, the next could be 1 cm, then 2.5 cm, or you could make one wider than the previous two.
^Got it. Then could you tell me how you drew the water?
^Of course! There are a few things to keep in mind. I wanted the water to look clear enough to see the bottom, so I started by drawing the objects underwater.

^Ripples distort the way those objects look, so you can make their lines a little wavy too. And since light can pass through the surface and spread underwater, you shouldn’t shade the whole thing too dark.
^Finally, I added the ripples on the surface where the duck had been swimming.
^Chris suddenly noticed that Tracy was getting happier and happier as she talked. She seemed much more cheerful than when they first met.
^That’s a really detailed explanation. Can I ask one last question?
^Because someone’s actually willing to talk to me about drawing! I’ve never talked about it with my friends before because I’m afraid they won’t be interested, or that they’ll find me annoying.
^Aren’t you worried I might find you annoying too?
^How would you know if you’ve never tried?
^You could talk about drawing with your family.?
^Then just talk to your friends about something else.
^So you can talk to me because we’re not friends?
cp04_o1: ^Uh... so you already think I’m annoying... I’m sorry.?
cp04_o2: ^I’d rather not risk it. What if they really do find me annoying? I don’t have many friends to begin with.
cp04_o3: ^I’m an only child, and all my parents ever do is work and nag me to finish my homework.
cp04_o4: ^But drawing is the only topic I can talk about for ages. When they talk about anything else, I mostly just listen.
^Well, at least you still get to spend time with your friends.
cp04_o5: ^Ah, no, that’s not what I meant... Uh... Actually, I guess that is kind of what I’m saying.
cp04_after: ^By the way, did you really understand everything I was talking about earlier?
^Huh? Weren’t you clever enough to trick me into admitting the truth earlier? Hahaha!.
^That’s only because you don’t talk to people much. You didn’t catch on.
^Then you should talk to me more often.
^I’ll pass. I’d rather hang out with my mates.
^How cold! We’ve been talking for so long, and I still don’t even know your name.
^I’m Tracy. Thanks for talking with me for so long! It felt really good to finally say all the things I’ve been keeping to myself.
^Wait! You’ve asked me so many questions. Can I ask you one?
^Why did you decide to come in and talk to me?
^I guess I was curious. I hardly ever go into the art classroom.
^Is that really all? Are you sure you didn’t fall for me while you were sneaking a look?
^Hahaha! Don’t go! Stay and chat a little longer~
^She looked so innocent, but she’s actually pretty sly. Guess you really can’t judge a book by its cover.
